text:
anita: Quick check — I ran a perturbation sweep on the new embed model (heron-lite-int6) vs baseline (heron-v1). Short summary below.

jon: paste the recall numbers?

anita: Baseline recall@10 (wiki_holdout, 10k queries): 0.842 ± 0.006 (bootstrapped 1k resamples).
Heron-lite-int6: 0.823 ± 0.007 -> ~-2.3% absolute.

lee: What's the noise injection setup?

anita: Three perturbation families: char-drop (p=0.05), random-word-insert, punctuation-strip. Each applied independently across queries.
Config snippet:```python
# run perturbation sweep
for pfn in [char_drop, random_insert, punct_strip]:
    results = run_eval(model, queries, perturb_fn=pfn, resamples=1000)
    report(results)
```

samuel: Did you check pairwise distance shift / centroid drift?

anita: Yes — mean intra-cluster cosine dropped baseline 0.68 -> 0.64 for int6.
Silhouette (k=100): baseline 0.31, int6 0.27.

jon: Any obvious query classes that fail?

anita: Short queries (<4 tokens) and punctuation-heavy queries show biggest regression.
Example failing query: "C++ vector push back" — nearest neighbors change top-5 in int6.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled for heron-lite-int6 on 3 nodes at 03:00UTC (canary label).

lee: Recommend rerun with per-channel quantization and a KV-cache-friendly quant profile. Also try small norm rescaling after quantization.

anita: Running per-channel next. Also doing a paired bootstrap diff to get p-value for recall delta.

samuel: Remember earlier we recovered ~50% of gap by scaling norms by ~1.04 on compact models. Worth a quick sweep.

anita: Tried +1.04 multiplier on normalized vectors -> recall@10 moved from 0.823 -> 0.829. Narrowed gap but not full recovery.

jon: Can you drop a reproducible script?

anita: Sure:```bash
./eval.sh --model heron-lite-int6 --holdout wiki_holdout_10k \\n  --perturbations char_drop,punct_strip --resamples 1000 --k 10
```

lee: Also add UMAP + sample-diff visualizations to the PR so we can inspect drift per-topic.

anita: Will add UMAP. Quick note from paired bootstrap: p=0.007 for recall@10 delta (paired) — so it's unlikely noise.

samuel: If per-channel doesn't close it, run ablations at 5/4 bits and profile latency+cost; maybe 6->5 bit gives better quality/cost tradeoff.

anita: Agreed. I'll run per-channel + 5-bit ablation and post numbers in ~2h.

jon: :eyes: Good work. If canary shows >3% degradation on production traces we should auto-revert.

anita: Adding a short-query routing filter that sends queries <4 tokens to baseline for the canary window.

lee: Nice mitigation. Keep logs small — include sample IDs for failed queries so we can human-review.

anita: Will do. Posting results when jobs finish. :thumbsup:
